### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ea8342ac1cf3c8742313eee38c1c9cc268bae7e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c35191804fa72cb4e44681d2876b4d07c6d62ec3` — the merge of head `301b4e3d8f13bae733c2cc5d3c9e4a516c0ef55a` into base `6ea8342ac1cf3c8742313eee38c1c9cc268bae7e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c35191804fa72cb4e44681d2876b4d07c6d62ec3 && git checkout c35191804fa72cb4e44681d2876b4d07c6d62ec3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ea8342ac1cf3c8742313eee38c1c9cc268bae7e 301b4e3d8f13bae733c2cc5d3c9e4a516c0ef55a && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ea8342ac1cf3c8742313eee38c1c9cc268bae7e && git merge --no-ff 301b4e3d8f13bae733c2cc5d3c9e4a516c0ef55a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ea8342ac1cf3c8742313eee38c1c9cc268bae7e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ea8342ac1cf3c8742313eee38c1c9cc268bae7e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

No conclusion is `failure` or `cancelled`.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff implies these accept-set and public-surface changes; each named right or wrong against the published spec (`ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldPatches`: "Display patches of the target object's own fields … which options exist stay the vendor's … A patch naming a field or option value the target does not have is refused at install and by `os validate`") and ADR-0146 D10 second rule (`options` membership is the vendor's; an extension changes a base field only within the display whitelist).

1. **The fold's option-patch accept set narrows to the owner's declared options.** `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` now asks `fieldPatchTargetMisses` BEFORE the merge, of `ownFieldsTarget(owner, ownFields, carried)`: the `own` contributor's stored declaration restricted to the own fields the merge will carry. An option only an extension's `fields` redeclaration adds (same extension or an earlier one) misses with `reason: 'option'`, is removed from the patch by `admittedFieldPatches`, and is named once by `reportFieldPatchMisses`. On `main` the judge read `merged` after the merge, so the same patch applied whenever the redeclarer folded first. **Right**: this is the spec's own refusal ("which options exist stay the vendor's"; "refused at install and by `os validate`") made real at the third reader, and the install door (`getObjectOwner(name).definition`) and `os validate` (the composed stack's declared object) were already judging that target; no door source moves. Pinned by the three new objectql cases (redeclarer first, same extension, patcher first), with the door's judge asked beside the fold in each.

2. **Which fields a patch reaches is unchanged.** `carried` admits an own field in the running body's record spelling or one this extension body redeclares, which is exactly the set `applyFieldPatches` applied on `main` (`ownFields.has(name)` plus `recordFieldOf(merged)`); `applyFieldPatches` keeps its `ownFields` guard. The array-spelled by-name fold pin (`foldObjectExtendersOnto` over an array-spelled body: not patched, named once) holds by the same reasoning: `recordFieldOf(running)` is undefined on array `fields`, the field is not carried, the judge reports `reason: 'field'`, and the warning text is the one `main` printed. **Right.**

3. **Field-key patches on a taken-over field still apply; owner-declared options still relabel onto the redeclared field.** Control case 4 pins `label: 'Sector'` and `tech`/`retail` relabels applied over the takeover, `finance` untouched. The judge's target is the owner's field, so an owner-declared option is admitted, and `patchedField` finds it on the merged (redeclared) field when the redeclaration kept it. **Right.**

4. **Naming is now the judge's verdict, not a second walk.** `reportFieldPatchMisses(misses, packageId)` names exactly the misses the judge returned, with the same `object|package|field|option` dedupe key and the same warning sentence; `miss.object` is `String(baseDefinition.name ?? extension.name ?? '')`, the string `main` built from `target.name`. **Right** for everything the judge misses. What the judge admits but the fold cannot apply is no longer named; that is the residual, judged in ④.

5. **No owner registered: nothing judged, nothing applied, nothing named.** `misses` is `[]` when `owner` or `ownFields` is undefined, the extension passes to `mergeObjectDefinitions` unchanged, and `applyFieldPatches` returns `fields` by reference on `!ownFields`. Same as `main`. **Right.**

6. **`admittedFieldPatches` is a pure filter of the judge's verdict.** A `field` miss deletes the whole patch; an `option` or `picklist-option` miss deletes that option entry (a picklist-bound field's option labels were already unreachable in `patchedField`, so this is naming-only parity). Returns `patches` by reference when nothing was missed, so the by-reference contract of `applyFieldPatches` ("returns `fields` BY REFERENCE when nothing applies") is preserved upstream. Two misses on one field (field miss then option miss) cannot co-occur from `fieldPatchTargetMisses` (it `continue`s after a field miss), and the loop tolerates it anyway. **Right.**

7. **`tenantPatchedDisplayKeys` (ADR-0029 D9.2a yield set) is unchanged and still reads every contributor's `fieldPatches`, dropped entries included.** A yield key for an option the fold now never applies is inert. **Right (no-op).**

8. **Public surface.** No export added, removed or re-typed in any package: `registry.ts` adds a type-only import of `FieldPatchTargetMiss` (already exported by `@objectstack/metadata-core`); `ownFieldsTarget`, `admittedFieldPatches` and `reportFieldPatchMisses` are module-private or `private`. `extension-field-patch-targets.ts` moves one docblock sentence and no code (`fieldPatchTargetMisses` body is byte-identical). No `packages/spec/**`, no new error code, no new gate, no door source change in `cloud-connection` or `cli`; the two door test additions pin an agreement that was green on `main` by construction (both doors already read the owner). **Right.**

9. **The install door and `os validate` accept sets do not move.** Read in the cited code: `fieldPatchTargetRefusalsOf` resolves `getTarget` to a delivered body or `registry.getObjectOwner(name).definition`; `findFieldPatchTargetRefusals` resolves it to the composed stack's declared objects. Neither reads the resolved (merged) object, before or after this PR. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/28809-field-patch-owner-declared-options.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` as line-initial declarations, a `BREAKING` banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) with its reasoning, a Before / Now / Who-sees-it account, and the one-line remedy ("set that option's label where the option is declared"). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, and the title carries `!`.

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` **matches the diff**: an input the fold accepted on `main` (an option patch of an extension-added option, redeclarer folded first) is no longer applied. Nothing is widened at any reader. Measured by the dev's red-first run (3 red with `registry.ts` at `663b7c08`), which I did not re-run; the check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the conservative and correct arm (AGENTS.md §3: "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`; several ⇒ `narrowed`"): what an author can write and have SERVED by a stack booted outside the install door (a programmatic `registerObject`, or a boot that never ran `os validate`) tightens. The kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves: `objectql` `minor` is **right**. A breaking changeset with its migration (the remedy line) and its ADR-0087 disposition in writing is present; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the registration reader) is green.
- No changeset for `@objectstack/metadata-core`: the only change is a docblock sentence; no emitted behaviour or type moves; `Check Changeset` on the head is green. Not owed. `cloud-connection` and `cli` are test-only.
- `Skills-docs: none` verified: `git grep fieldPatches` over `skills/**` and `.claude/skills/**` at the head returns nothing.
- One accuracy slip, should-fix S2 below: the changeset's "Before" and "Who sees it" name only an option "an extension's `fields` redeclaration adds". On `main` the judge's target was `merged`, which starts from `overlay ?? own`, so an option a tenant overlay base added to an owner field was also admitted at the fold and is also dropped now (the doors refused it already). The declared arm and level are unaffected.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` (dev): the residual case is silent at the fold; `main` named it; naming it "needs a new rule".** Answered in ④ as **should-fix S1**, not a must-fix. It is not a new rule: `main`'s own naming walk (the judge over the merged target, naming only, never dropping) restores it in the fold with the admission unchanged.
- **PR body, Acceptance notes: `origin/main` moved 10 commits since the gates; `git merge-tree` clean; seat 1's PR #28811 (also `registry.ts`) not landed.** At review time the PR reports `mergeable: true` on `main` `892eb668`; the claim's serial constraint stands (whichever lands second merges `main` once). No action owed here.
- **Dev flag: CI on PR #28836 was not awaited.** Now answered by the head's check-runs: all 50 completed, none red.
- **Card body's measure-first condition** ("Measure first whether any shipped package or example has an extension redeclaring an owner field through `fields`"): reported as 0 packages or examples declaring `fieldPatches` at all; consistent with the changeset's "Who sees it". Taken as the dev's measurement; nothing in the diff contradicts it.
- **Card dedupe note: #28655 item A (domain:spec, open) stays out.** Confirmed: no `packages/spec/**` in the diff; the same-extension case is pinned here at the fold and the door only.
- **`Thread-read: none`, `Resume-from: none` on the claim.** No cross-thread carry to check.
- No other dev flag; `out_of_scope_findings` is empty.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the cited code at the head.

**Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The spec declares `fieldPatches` as display patches of "the target object's own fields" whose "options … stay the vendor's", and promises that "a patch naming a field or option value the target does not have is refused at install and by `os validate`". ADR-0146 D10 refuses `options` membership on an extension outright. An option that exists only because an extension replaced the owner's field through `fields` is not the vendor's option; relabelling it through `fieldPatches` was never a declared capability, and `content/docs` on `main` already told the author to set that text "where it is declared". The fold was the one reader serving it, by priority accident (the redeclarer had to fold first). The head makes the spec's own refusal real at the third reader with the same judge and the same target the two doors use, which is exactly the card's "one answer at all three readers". The route chosen (fold reads the owner, not doors reading the merged field) is the only one the spec admits: the doors cannot see another package's extension at install or validate time, and the spec says the options are the vendor's.

**Breaking attempts, read in the tree:**

- *Priority inversion.* Takeover at 300 after a patcher at 200 patching an owner option: the patch applies onto the owner's field, then the takeover replaces the field whole and the patch is lost. Same on `main`; that is `fields`' declared "replaced, not merged" semantics, not this PR's.
- *Owner field picklist-bound, extension redeclares it with inline options plus `finance`, patch of `finance`.* Owner target is picklist-bound → `picklist-option` miss → dropped and named; doors say the same. Consistent.
- *Overlay base.* The fold's base is `overlay ?? own`; the judge now reads `owner`, never the overlay. A tenant overlay that ADDS an option to an owner field: patch of it was applied on `main`, dropped and named now; both doors already refused it. Consistent and spec-true, but the changeset should name it (S2). A tenant overlay that DROPS an owner option: same residual as below, by a second route.
- *No owner, extension only.* Unchanged, nothing applied or named.
- *By-name fold over an array-spelled body.* Unchanged, pinned.
- *The `carried` closure captures `running` (the pre-merge `merged`) and `extension` (post audit/queue governance), and the merge is fed `admitted`, which spreads the same `extension`.* The judge and the merge see one body. No drift.
- *Warning text for an extension-added option* reads "names an option `crm_account.industry` does not have … this field's are `tech`, `retail`" — the owner's list, which is what the author must address. Accurate at the fold now, and identical to the door's sentence.

**The residual (card ruling 4 / dev's open question).** An earlier layer (an extension's `fields` redeclaration at lower priority, or a tenant overlay base) drops an owner-declared option; a later extension patches that option. All three readers admit it, because the owner declares it. `applyFieldPatches` finds no such option on the merged field, so nothing of the option entry applies; the patch's field keys still apply. On `main` the fold named it (`reportFieldPatchMisses` over the merged target); on the head it is silent, and the head's docs and changeset declare the silence.

Judged **should-fix S1, not a must-fix**, for these reasons:
- No accept set disagrees: this is the one answer the card wanted, and the residual is admitted everywhere.
- No misleading text reaches a screen: the option is absent from the served field entirely (the takeover's choice), so the author sees the option gone, not a stale label. The harm the naming existed for ("the author reads Sector, the screen keeps Industry") does not arise.
- The spec's refusal clause is about "a field or option value the target does not have"; the owner target HAS it. So the silence contradicts no published spec sentence and no ADR-0146 D10 sentence; it narrows only the `main` docs' "an unmatched patch … is named once in the log", and the head's docs re-declare that corner explicitly rather than leaving it silent.
- It is cheap to restore and it is not a new rule: after `mergeObjectDefinitions`, ask the same judge of the admitted patches against `ownFieldsTarget` over the merged body for NAMING only (never dropping, never refusing), as `main` did, and dedupe under the same key. The fold then keeps "what it names is what it skipped", the invariant `main`'s `ownFieldsTarget` docblock stated. Either land that, or keep the declared silence and fix the changeset sentence (S1's minimum).

**Findings:**

- **S1 (should-fix).** The residual silent no-op. Preferred: restore `main`'s naming of an admitted-but-inapplicable option patch (judge the admitted patches once more over the merged target, naming only). Minimum: the changeset's "Residual, unchanged rule" bullet is wrong as written: the admission rule is unchanged, but the fold's naming of this case changed (`main` named it, the head does not), and that is part of what the narrowing publishes. Say so, and widen the residual's cause to "an earlier layer that leaves the option out", since a tenant overlay base reaches it too.
- **S2 (should-fix).** Changeset and PR body "Before" / "Who sees it": the dropped-at-the-fold set also includes an option a tenant overlay base adds to an owner field (the `main` target was `merged`, which starts from `overlay ?? own`). The doors already refused it, so the arm and level stand; the account of who sees the change should name it.
- No must-fix.
